quirks.description: Properties set under the keys "0", "1", ... in order make a PHP list, so the store encodes as a JSON array instead of an object.
quirks.case: StoreTest.json#a list of properties encodes as a JSON array

quirks.description: setVersion() accepts only the nine lowercase SHA names, but hash() passes the stored `version` option to PHP's hash(), which takes any case and other algorithms (md5, sha512/256).
quirks.case: ShaTest.json#the version option goes to hash()

quirks.description: Integer option keys (a JSON object with numeric keys) reach Hash::setOption(string $key) under strict types and raise a TypeError whose message quotes the PHP file and line.
`iteration_count_log2` goes through PHP arithmetic: numeric strings work, other strings and arrays raise "Unsupported operand types".
quirks.case: PHPassTest.json#iteration counts from options are juggled

quirks.description: A JSON `[]` header or claims segment decodes to an empty PHP array and passes the "must be a JSON object" check.
Only empty-string audience identifiers are rejected; integers and other non-strings are accepted and signed.
A nonce, access token or code of "0" counts as absent (in_array against [null, '', '0']).
quirks.case: IdTokenTest.json#empty and zero nonce, access token and code are absent

quirks.description: `!empty($parts['host'])` treats a host of "0" as missing, so https://0/x is not an absolute URI.
password_verify() recomputes with a canonicalised 22nd salt character, so a stored $2a$ hash with a non-canonical one never verifies.
The salt "0" is rejected as empty (PHP's falsy string).

deviations.php: The hash in use is found by object identity: the instance returned by getHashByName() can be passed to setHash(), and one instance can be registered under several names, each then guarded as current by removeHash().
deviations.reason: Rust's registry owns its hashes: Password::use_hash(name) selects a registered one (removeHash() guards that name) and set_hash() takes an unregistered copy; one value cannot be registered twice.

deviations.php: Returns the shared instance, so setters called on it change the hash the proof (and a Password registry) uses.
deviations.reason: Rust returns a borrow: Proof::hasher_mut() (and Password::hash_by_name_mut()) change it in place instead.

deviations.php: webauthn-lib's StringStream fread()s a CBOR byte or text string's declared length before checking it, so a credential declaring a string larger than PHP's memory_limit ends the process with a fatal "Allowed memory size exhausted" error.
deviations.reason: Rust reads only the bytes present and reports the same "Out of range. Expected: N, read: M." error webauthn-lib raises for lengths that fit in memory.
